title: IIHF files challenge with CAS over decision to reinstate Russia based on nondisclosure: Source
content:
The International Ice Hockey Federation filed a challenge with the Court of Arbitration for Sport over its decision to reinstate Russia to the governing body’s competitions, an IIHF source, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss matters of a sensitive nature, confirmed to The Athletic on Friday.

The IIHF’s challenge is based on the nondisclosure of ties to Russia by two of the three CAS panel members responsible for the decision, according to the source.

TSN broadcaster Gord Miller first reported the news on social media.

The first tournament impacted by the CAS’ decision, issued Oct. 30, is the World Junior Championship, which begins in the Canadian province of Alberta on Dec. 26.

The Government of Canada confirmed Wednesday that it would not grant visas to Russian players, staff and officials for the event, effectively guaranteeing that the Russian team would not participate.

“As (Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney) has said, as long as Russia and Belarus are supporting the war in Ukraine, athletes representing those countries will not be permitted to compete for their countries in Canada. With respect to the 2026 World Junior Championship specifically, Russian athletes will not participate,” Adam van Koeverden, Canada’s secretary of state for sport, said in a statement released Wednesday.

Additionally, the Canadian government “will take measures to individually assess and prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering Canada to compete, regardless of whether they already hold valid visas,” van Koeverden said.

Several national federations in the field for the tournament had said they would not compete against a Russian team if it were allowed to return to international competition.

After the World Juniors, the next major IIHF tournament is U18 men’s worlds, scheduled to begin April 21 in Minnesota.
